review.translation: [And|0] [I|6] [will|5] [also|0] [judge|5] [the nation|2,1] [that|3] [they will serve|4], [and after|7] [that|8] [they will come out|9] [with|10] [great|11] [possessions|10].

analysis.evidence: אֶת marks the focused phrase as the direct object of דָּן (“will judge”), and אָנֹכִי (“I”) is the subject. The speaker says that the nation they will serve also comes under his judgment.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The additive particle גַם means “also” and focuses on אֶת הַגּוֹי אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ (“the nation that they will serve”).
Hebrew direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The relative clause אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ identifies the nation that Abram’s descendants will serve. אֶת marks that nation as the object of God’s judgment.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: a people counted as a nation

analysis.evidence: In הַגּוֹי אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ, “the nation that they will serve,” אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause in which הַגּוֹי supplies the understood object of יַעֲבֹדוּ.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected Hebrew relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Abram’s descendants are the subject of יַעֲבֹדוּ. The relative clause אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ identifies הַגּוֹי as the nation they will serve. God says he will judge that nation, after which the descendants will leave.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural, with future reference.

analysis.evidence: The object marker אֶת introduces הַגּוֹי אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ, “the nation they will serve.” With that object placed first, דָּן אָנֹכִי means “I will judge that nation.”
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute. The independent pronoun אָנֹכִי supplies the first-person subject, and the prediction gives the participle future force.

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 69377:13, 67332:4, 66569:12, 66314:8.
analysis.morphology: Independent personal pronoun, first person common singular, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן means “and after that.” It places the departure expressed by יֵצְאוּ after the judgment announced in דָּן אָנֹכִי.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ (“and”) prefixes אַחֲרֵי, the preposition governing כֵן (“that”).

analysis.evidence: In וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן יֵצְאוּ, כֵן refers back to the judgment just announced. The phrase means “and after that they will go out.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected adverb with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The plural subject of יֵצְאוּ is the same group who will serve the nation in אֲשֶׁר יַעֲבֹדוּ. וְאַחֲרֵי כֵן places their departure after God judges that nation, and בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל says they will leave with great possessions. This sequence identifies the promised exodus.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine plural. The subject is Abram’s descendants, and the verb predicts their departure.
analysis.sense: go out of Egypt in the exodus

draft.change: Add the root רכש and its noun רְכוּשׁ for acquired possessions. The source’s personal-name gloss does not fit this occurrence.
draft.definition: Property or goods that someone owns, taken collectively.
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:5 pairs רְכוּשָׁם, “their possessions,” with רָכָשׁוּ, “they had acquired.”

analysis.evidence: יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל means “they will leave with great wealth.” The masculine singular adjective גָּדוֹל agrees with רְכֻשׁ, the property they will take with them.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בִּ means “with” and prefixes a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In יֵצְאוּ בִּרְכֻשׁ גָּדוֹל, “they will go out with great wealth,” גָּדוֹל describes the amount of wealth they will take with them.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute adjective agreeing with רְכֻשׁ, the noun it follows.
